Research programme

Quantum holography and associative chiral Koszul duality

Ordered collisions, chiral quantum groups, and the relation between boundary operators and bulk theories.

Last updated 16 November 2026

Associative chiral Koszul duality studies singular composition with the order of the inputs retained. Its constructions include coefficient systems on configurations, vertex algebras, quantum vertex algebras, and module categories with fusion. Bar and cobar relate multiplication to coherent comultiplication. A realization by fields must also specify the collision maps, completion, , and module tensor product.

The programme has coefficient dualities, explicit field duals, algebraic bulk operations, and restricted fusion theorems. Several comparisons now hold on full algebraic state spaces or at every finite configuration arity. Their hypotheses distinguish polynomial states, completed inputs, ordinary derived categories, and categories defined by different weak equivalences.

The remaining questions compare independently defined constructions. They concern native collision operations, common completed fusion domains, geometric bulk actions, and states prepared by physical amplitudes. A complementary-level partner, a bar dual, and a vacuum endomorphism algebra retain separate definitions.

The table gives the available results and the unresolved comparison for each example. The questions below state the mathematical data needed to extend them. A partial theorem retains its positive domain even when a stronger comparison fails.

Status

How to read the status marks

Proved and independently checked
An independently checked proof establishes exactly the stated scope. Publication status and published antecedents are separate.
Conditional
The conclusion is proved under an explicitly named hypothesis that remains unproved.
Open problem
The stated construction or comparison remains unresolved.
Published
An existing result in the literature, with its author, source and year given. Its hypotheses remain those of the cited result.
Partly established
A restricted case, a related theorem or an obstruction is established; the full mathematical question represented by the column remains unresolved.
Not yet formulated
No precise version of this mathematical question is formulated for the example.
Refuted as first posed
The proposed form is ruled out by a proved counterexample or obstruction. Any replacement is stated with its own hypotheses.
Proposed
A proposed construction has a written argument, with the stated unresolved proof obligations.

Then BIB_I is a factorization algebra, and its canonical connection and residue operation reconstruct a unital chiral algebra on the right differential module ωX⊗B{1}\omega_X\otimes B_{\{1\}}, with all operadic substitutions. What would change the programme

Constructions that would change the programme

The most consequential gaps are maps between independently defined theories: from coefficient duals to singular fields and modules, from boundary operations to physical bulk observables, and from scalar traces to prepared states. The questions below give concrete tests for those maps and for major advances in the individual families. A successful test settles the component stated; the full target still requires its other operations, domains and coherences.

1

A native Koszul interface with collisions

Open problem

Construct a filtered realization of the transverse relative bar or module-Hom of independently defined endpoint modules, and compare its continuous dual with the . The comparison must preserve the positive filtration, actual module-linear mapping complexes, numerical and Jordan charge sectors, the distinct and occupied vacuum, both ordered binary charts, spectral and the total position connection. It must induce the original field comparison and the independently normalized associator. The first deciding construction is the regular/localized/supported Taylor square with both derived vacuum specializations; extend it to the 13|213|2 branch before asserting a common collision theory.

Why it matters

This would connect associative coefficient duality to independently defined fields, endpoints and fusion on the same domains. It would make the line algebra a description of the native interface rather than only a one-position algebra. Analytic specialization and physical generation would still require their own comparisons.

What is proved toward it2 statements
Proved and independently checked

Two point-kernel theories are already distinguished

For the polynomial Heisenberg point algebra, the ordinary derived kernel is the local-cohomology coring RΓ(t)ℂ[t]R\Gamma_{(t)}\mathbb C[t], with image the tt-power-supported sector. A separate product-bar/hybrid homotopy–derived enhancement has the diagonal Koszul coring and retains every algebraic unbounded charged complex and all module-linear maps. Finite independent point tensors and the specified polynomial, fixed-field and energy-product bounds are established. These point kernels do not yet supply actions and balanced unit/counit for the unaugmented geometric transverse monoid.

Proved and independently checked

Separated charge transport has finite higher operations

On fully separated configurations, the reduced exterior model has a strictly unital finite A∞A_\infty automorphism and inverse, with finite insertions for arbitrary finite commuting charge matrices, including Jordan blocks. The absolute spectral cocycle is interpreted by rational substitutions before a common Laurent expansion. The formal comparison criterion retains its full normalized universal Maurer–Cartan hypothesis; it does not supply the missing supported Taylor target or a finite numerical-charge homotopy for an unspecified comparison.

2

Supported bulk operations and their global recipient

Open problem

For the universal affine cochain system with nondegenerate shifted form β=κ+Kill⁡/2\beta=\kappa+\operatorname{Kill}/2, construct the regular, localized and supported configuration-operation complexes carrying the native product, the specified secondary operation and an independently defined boundary action. Solve the relative four-face equations δF4=E4\delta F_4=E_4, rF4−δG4=hproperrF_4-\delta G_4=h_{\mathrm{proper}} on 12|3|412|3|4 and 12|3412|34 in that actual recipient, with the prescribed separated homotopy. In the mixed-current realization, retain the original unrestricted global distribution domain and its branch-support data; a germ comparison or a globally bounded normal-order replacement does not settle it. The next mixed-current construction must select its intermediate-state object independently, carry actual supported products and arbitrary cut changes on that object, and retain the new normal classes under the required coefficient and completion maps.

Why it matters

This would identify which higher operations belong to a native bulk and how they act on the boundary. It is a necessary bridge from state-level formulas to local observables and reconstruction. The actual actor category must be specified; representability in an algebraic category already excluded by a no-go theorem cannot be assumed.

What is proved toward it2 statements
Proved and independently checked

The full projected affine fields agree on algebraic states

For finite-dimensional complex 𝔤\mathfrak g, universal balanced affine vacua and absolute ghosts, the specified projected two-copy fields agree on every algebraic state, including regular coefficients. The primary equality requires no inverse form. With invertible β\beta, the secondary agrees on all algebraic ghost jets with the endpoint-average operation. Some current-containing inputs fail the distinct residue comparison, so this does not identify the full native supported action.

Proved and independently checked

The full scalar global answer retains three escaping modules

For ordinary scalar mixed distributions with finite order on each compact and no uniform global normal-order bound, the three-position complex has H2(ℐ)=ℰu⊕︎ℰs⊕︎ℰv⊕︎jAP⊕︎jSP,s=u+v.H^2(\mathcal I)=\mathcal E_u\oplus\mathcal E_s\oplus\mathcal E_v\oplus j_AP\oplus j_SP,\qquad s=u+v. Here PP is the joint point principal-part module and jA,jSj_A,j_S are the two forest inclusions. Each ℰx\mathcal E_x is the specified locally finite Dolbeault cokernel; it vanishes after restriction to a smaller normal radius. The scalar finite-pole vacuum map has exactly the two forest modules as its degree-two image and ℰu⊕︎ℰs⊕︎ℰv\mathcal E_u\oplus\mathcal E_s\oplus\mathcal E_v as cokernel. The forest sum is intrinsically the simultaneous u,vu,v-locally-nilpotent submodule and gives the unique polynomial-Weyl-linear section. This is algebraic scalar cohomology. The finite-normal complex and the normal germ limit have different answers; state-valued and all-position recognition remain open.

3

Full base change in the centre construction

Open problem

In the strict category of algebraic dg vertex superalgebras with ordinary tensors, take the nonzero-level Heisenberg algebra A=VκA=V_\kappa, B=Λ(ϵ)B=\Lambda(\epsilon) and CB=B⊗AC_B=B\otimes A. Determine whether the required base transitions on the full two-legged cocycle categories GdG_d induce nerve weak equivalences, with unrestricted sources and refinements. Targets retain their prescribed bounded-below energy grading and zero-mode nilpotence, with every admissible target link. For the split base U=A⋉(B⊗D)U=A\ltimes(B\otimes D), D=(P→L→Q)D=(P\to L\to Q) acyclic, the first exact question is whether NGdUr↪NGdUNG^r_{d_U}\hookrightarrow NG_{d_U} is a weak equivalence. Here r:U→Ar:U\to A, and tameness means that the ideal generated by the image of ker⁡r\ker r is acyclic. Why it matters

This would settle a precise step from coefficient cocycles to the full centre comparison. It would determine whether unrestricted actors are captured by the tame construction. The physical action and annulus theorem would still require independent maps.

What is proved toward it2 statements

Surjective transitions identify the tame subcategory

For a surjective base arrow a:d→d′a:d\to d', let IgI_g be the dg vertex ideal generated by h(ker⁡a)h(\ker a). Quotienting by IgI_g gives NGd′≃NGdaNG_{d'}\simeq NG_d^a, where GdaG_d^a is the full subcategory with acyclic IgI_g; the full transition is this equivalence followed by inclusion. 4

An interface compatible with principal reduction

Open problem

For 𝔰𝔩2\mathfrak{sl}_2 and t≠0t\ne0, raw affine levels t−2t-2 and −t−2-t-2, and c(t)=13−6(t+t−1)c(t)=13-6(t+t^{-1}), construct an independent defect reduction and a natural comparison DSlineΨaff≃ΨVirDSaff.\mathrm{DS}_{\mathrm{line}}\Psi_{\mathrm{aff}}\simeq\Psi_{\mathrm{Vir}}\mathrm{DS}_{\mathrm{aff}}. Prove the actual source/image and enhanced weak-equivalence conditions. Retain the coherent two-action kernel, paired constraint characters, ghost polarization, topology and shifts, and match the reduced augmentation to the contragredient universal vacuum at 26−c(t)26-c(t). The first test is the actual marked counit/augmentation square with the anti-action signs; then compare native binary , position connections and collision faces.

Why it matters

The exterior actor Λ(ξ)\Lambda(\xi), |ξ|=1|\xi|=1, has a discrete k2k^2 torsor of final binary fillers. Nonconstant or nonpropagating sources, independently prescribed reverse cuts, uniform-source secondary data and higher coherent assembly remain before full recognition.

Proved and independently checked

Surjective base change and the tame cocycle subcategory

Over ℂ\mathbb C, retain the nonzero-level rank-one Heisenberg boundary, the exterior actor B=Λ(ϵ)B=\Lambda(\epsilon) with |ϵ|=1|\epsilon|=1 and dϵ=Tϵ=0d\epsilon=T\epsilon=0, ordinary algebraic tensors and localization at state quasi-isomorphisms. For a surjective base arrow a:d→d′a:d\to d^{\prime} in the specified Heisenberg action comparison, let GdaG_d^a be the full subcategory where the dg vertex ideal generated by h(ker⁡a)h(\ker a) is acyclic. Quotienting by that ideal proves NGd′≃NGda,N G_{d^{\prime}}\simeq N G_d^a, preserving both cocycle legs, all refinements and every admissible target link. A base section retracts the full transition and makes it injective on components and all based homotopy groups. The displayed split object and specified pullbacks are tame. The remaining inclusion NGda→NGdN G_d^a\to N G_d is still undecided, including higher homotopy even if every component meets the tame subcategory. A functorial incoming tame refinement c(g)→gc(g)\to g would suffice and can be made surjective by a mapping-path construction. Relative free/PBW exactness is one possible method, not a necessary or equivalent criterion. The ideal-valued monotonicity test only excludes outgoing arrows to tame objects; it excludes neither incoming refinements nor zigzags. Non-surjective and full required transitions, λB\lambda_B, the separate nilpotent inclusion and the actual qBq_B comparison remain open.

7

Fusion on a common completed module domain

Open problem

Extend the ordered Heisenberg completed-input products beyond the proved finite-diagonal and retained-leg domains. Establish arbitrary third-level strictness for infinite coefficient spaces, intrinsic recovery of the separate leg actions, compatible chamber transport, and module units. Then compare the completed with independent geometric fusion and exchange.

Why it matters

The first two recursive completion levels preserve the admitted quasi-isomorphisms. Fixed finite trees also have exactness on their admitted inputs. The next completion step needs a new strictness argument.

8

A common nonrational coefficient category

Open problem

Construct one positioned coefficient category containing the required rational, multiplicative, elliptic and monodromic fields, with genuine mixed tensors, independent colour-resolved binary operations, collision descent, supported cut/unit/normal maps, full-turn holonomy and reconstruction. Use the established local/formal all-polynomial elliptic cubic field through ℂ[ℏ]/(ℏ4)\mathbb C[\hbar]/(\hbar^4) as an instance, retaining its actual lower fields and admitted all-state exchange. Construct its marked KZ/associator and native/global comparison maps, and solve the separate all-polynomial quartic and higher-order extension problems on explicit domains.

Why it matters

The elliptic branch now supplies an actual local/formal cubic quantum vertex algebra on all polynomial jets, beyond the exchange calculation. The remaining programme arrows are the common coefficient category, native supported operations, marked instance maps and higher precision.

9

Quantum operations with the required higher source terms

Open problem

Extend the nonabelian polar exchange to the fifth parameter coefficient and then to all orders. Separately, construct the common continuous higher-operad comparison with its inverse after changing the permitted unary and wheel data. Retain the essential higher classical source operations forced by the Lie-arity-four obstruction.

Why it matters

Parameter order and configuration arity are independent. Existing all-finite collision families do not raise the precision of the quantum exchange.

10

The full supported gravitational stress operation

Open problem

Construct a differential-stable admissible diagram for independently resolved roots, their normal derivatives, collision faces, and quantum companions. Compare it with the independently prescribed stress action on one common test domain. Extend the supported weight-five construction through weight nine, then compare the native all-depth line and its boundary endpoint.

Why it matters

The ordinary first-jet source square, two independent holomorphic jets and selected normal-relative, complete-endpoint and tangential-overlap operations now exist. The full admissible class and correction quotient, all normal operations and independent-height-ratio collar still need a common analytic diagram.

11

The relative cubic map in free elliptic reduction

Open problem

Construct the cubic comparison on the full intersection with the lower maps fixed. Extend the established joint two-root relation rows to the actual remaining polynomial and exterior history words. Construct the compact endpoint and independent projected, localization and harmonic comparisons, then verify every term of the attachment equation. Retain all anchor triples, normal directions, and branch intersections.

Why it matters

The specified relation rows now admit arbitrary finite right jets, and the marked all-top s and bare eta rows have their actual source equations and faces. These partials do not construct every history word, the compact endpoint or the independent projected arrows.

12

Global arithmetic positivity and its field trace

Open problem

Prove positivity of the complete Weil form on arbitrary compact support intervals, or construct a negative test for that complete functional. Independently construct an integral collision and trace comparison preserving Frobenius, normal directions, both endpoint actions, and every prime-power contribution. A positive geometric realization must give the prescribed full Gram identity on common domains.

Why it matters

Finite-window positivity and integral normal/Frobenius maps are established. The remaining signed estimates and native operation maps are separate mathematical requirements.

What the columns mean
Algebra and geometry
The field algebra or geometric coefficient object, with its multiplication, collision maps, exchange and vacuum.
Koszul dual
The dual construction, its curvature and completion, the category in which it lives, and any biduality or complementary-parameter statement.
Module comparison
A functor or equivalence between explicitly defined representation categories, including their weak equivalences and distinguished vacuum objects.
Fusion and exchange
Products of representations at moving points, associators, braiding, and reconstruction from a fibre functor.
Bulk operations
Local bulk observables or a candidate algebra of vacuum endomorphisms, together with higher operations and their boundary action.
Lines and endpoints
Line defects, their endpoint modules and couplings, and flat connections governing their motion.
States and sewing
State spaces and preparation by amplitudes, with the analytic or formal domains needed for gluing.
Physical comparison
Source and Ward identities, parameter normalization, and comparisons with a bulk theory defined independently of the boundary algebra.

Quantum Hamiltonian reduction Hf0H_f^0 is a braided tensor equivalence between the category of finite direct sums of affine Weyl modules 𝕍λk\mathbb V^k_\lambda, induced from finite-dimensional simple 𝔤\mathfrak g-modules of dominant integral highest weight λ\lambda, and the category of finite direct sums of their reductions as Wk(𝔤,f)W^k(\mathfrak g,f)-modules. The reduced category is rigid, with Hf0(𝕍λ∗k)H_f^0(\mathbb V^k_{\lambda^*}) dual to Hf0(𝕍λk)H_f^0(\mathbb V^k_\lambda), where λ∗\lambda^* labels the dual finite-dimensional representation.

Reference: Creutzig–Dhillon–Nakatsuka, The Kazhdan–Lusztig category of W-algebras of simply-laced Lie algebras at irrational levels (arXiv:2603.04667) (2026), Theorems 1.1 and 5.2; §§2.1–2.2.

Irrational W₃ sector cohomology

For K∈ℂ∖ℚK\in\mathbb C\setminus\mathbb Q and dominant integral 𝔰𝔩3\mathfrak{sl}_3 labels, the explicit paired W3W_3 BRST complex has zero cohomology away from the corrected partner labels. On the partner, its cohomology is one-dimensional in each of degrees 0,3,5,80,3,5,8 and zero otherwise. The proof uses the nonzero primitive-cover transgression from the Jantzen connecting map and the unique on-shell coresolution column; the bottom differential is its transferred projection. This is a graded-vector-space theorem. It does not construct sector multiplication, a two-row vertex algebra, a braid-reversed equivalence, arbitrary-module derived Hom or a rational-level extension.

Proved and independently checked

Matrix trigonometric fields in the multiplicative ring

In characteristic zero, the homogeneous matrix RTT construction gives integral divided fields, exchange, level-changing coproducts, and cut residues at every finite formal precision. Its spectral values lie in the completed multiplicative ring k[x±1,(x−1)−1]k[x^{\pm1},(x-1)^{-1}], with x=ezx=e^z. Already at second precision, the displayed form does not belong to the additive Laurent-polynomial ring. A common rational, trigonometric, and monodromic theory must therefore retain the value ring, translation, and positioned tensor maps.

Proved and independently checked

Binary Ward data do not determine a charged field family

For the translated rational-current module with κλν≠0\kappa\lambda\nu\ne0, one selected inserted primary admits the specified binary construction on every polynomial second input and for every current mode. Its free scalar and shift data can give either an ordinary Laurent example with trivial full turn or the normalized Kummer and Gaussian examples in their larger coefficient algebras. Translation and binary Ward commutators alone therefore do not force the Gaussian monodromy. Fields of arbitrary inserted descendants, vacuum normalization, coherent charge families and ternary collision identities remain separate constraints.

Proved and independently checked

Necessary conditions for full RTT recognition

In characteristic zero, at nonzero deformation parameter and rank at least two, the fundamental tensor square in the specified full RTT category is absolutely simple and has only scalar endomorphisms. The constant RTT coefficient equation is an identity over arbitrary coefficient algebras; it does not force commutativity. Any compatible Laurent presentation through an exact faithful monoidal fibre must send the fundamental exchange to a polynomial matrix with polynomial inverse and determinant one. These are necessary conditions. A full noncommutative cocycle, additive translation frame and comparison on every finite comodule remain unconstructed.

It retains the original midpoint second-order symbol and K=r02/8−r0′/2K=r_0^2/8-r_0^{\prime}/2, together with the exact admitted normalized all-state cubic exchange. The four-factor and product-pole arguments give actual generating locality with a collision bound independent of spectator polynomial degree and jet orders, and reconstruction gives weak associativity on all polynomial states with independent jets and full outputs. Admitted exchange retains finite meromorphic state span per input, vacuum, shifts, period laws, unitarity and both cubic hexagons. The normalized zero homogeneous exchange correction does not solve the distinct quartic Yang–Baxter equation.

Let AA be a fixed ordinary unital Beilinson–Drinfeld chiral algebra on a smooth separated complex curve. Its ordinary coefficient-family categories admit finite-map, collision, and insertion functors over arbitrary classical parameter schemes.
